subject: Unit economics deep dive / pricing follow-up (FintechX)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unit economics deep dive / pricing follow-up (FintechX)

Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from today's discovery and a few follow-ups so we can build the unit-econ model you asked for: 

Key takeaways (please confirm):
- Primary use case: conversational assistant + smart routing for customer support and two personalization features (contextual suggestions, session summarization).
- Expected avg monthly volume: ~30M tokens/month in month 1, growing to ~80M by month 6 (spiky distribution; peak concurrent requests expected during US business hours).
- Target P50 latency: <200ms for short-turn interactions; P95 <800ms for longer context flows.
- Acceptance criteria: under $/1M tokens target they mentioned during the call (we captured an initial target range but need exact number).

Questions/asks for you:
1) Can you confirm the target $/1M tokens you want us to model against? (You mentioned a ballpark on the call; want to be explicit.)
2) Can you share a rough breakdown of tokens per feature (support messages vs personalization vs summaries)? Even % splits work.
3) Any internal CAC / revenue-per-feature goals we should align to (for feature-level margin calc)?

Next steps from our side: Rishi and Vivek will build a quick unit-econ workbook showing cost per feature, recommended model/quantization profile, and required budget to meet target $/1M. Attaching our unit_econ_model.xlsx template — please drop numbers in the highlighted cells. We'll follow up with a short call to walk the numbers.

Attachments: unit_econ_model.xlsx (template)

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0191

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>

Date: 2026-07-03T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unit economics deep dive / pricing follow-up (FintechX)

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the template. Quick answers to your asks: 

1) Target $/1M tokens: Our procurement lead carved out a budget target of $4,500 per 1M tokens for the first year. We know that sounds aggressive; we want to understand tradeoffs (quantization, model choice, caching) to see if that is feasible.
2) Token split (rough, high-level):
   - Support assistant (primary): 60% of tokens
   - Session summarization: 20%
   - Contextual suggestions/personalization: 20%
3) CAC / revenue assumptions: Our LTV/CAC goal is 6x; initial pilot revenue contribution is estimated at $120k ARR if we hit performance goals. We need feature-level margin >40% after inference cost to consider expanding.

I've attached the internal usage spreadsheet with a couple of sample days — call out if you need anything else.

— Alex

On Fri, Jul 03, 2026 at 09:45 Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Got it — thanks for the detail. Rishi/Vivek will run scenarios and share a model.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-04T11:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unit economics deep dive / pricing follow-up (FintechX)

Alex / team — thanks for the numbers, that's helpful. A few clarifying questions before we finalize scenarios: 

1) Peak concurrency / qps during support spikes? (This materially affects batching gains and required pool sizing.)
2) Are you open to a mixed-model approach (smaller cheaper decoder for suggestions + larger tuned model for assistant), or do you prefer a single-model deployment?
3) Are session summaries allowed to be async (slightly higher latency) to further reduce cost, or must they be synchronous?

Initial thinking based on $4,500/1M target and 30M tokens/month:
- Raw inference cost target implies ~ $135k/mo inference spend cap at target pricing (30 * $4.5k).
- To hit >40% feature margin given your ARR estimates, we can show a few levers: model quantization (int8/qlora-ish), aggressive prefix caching for support flows, and client-side rate shaping for non-critical summary jobs.

We'll run three scenarios:
A) Conservative (higher perf) — higher cost, lower risk
B) Balanced — target-aligned with a mix of caching & quantization
C) Aggressive (cost-first) — likely lower latency guarantees, lower cost

We'll attach the scenario outputs and a one-page recommendation. Can we schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review? I can include our Solutions Engineer (Vivek) to go over concurrency and model choices.

— Rishi

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechx.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-05T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unit economics deep dive / pricing follow-up (FintechX)

Alex / Priya — attaching the completed unit econ workbook and a short pricing proposal based on the three scenarios Rishi outlined. Highlights: 

- Scenario A (Conservative): Estimated $/1M tokens = $6,800 — better P95 latency, recommended for pilot if SLA is strict.
- Scenario B (Balanced): Estimated $/1M tokens = $4,400 — uses mixed-model routing + int8 quantization + caching; aligns to your $4,500 target.
- Scenario C (Aggressive): Estimated $/1M tokens = $3,200 — cost-first; uses heavier quantization and async summaries; lower latency guarantees.

Feature-level example (month 1, 30M tokens overall):
- Support assistant (60% = 18M tokens): cost (Scenario B) ~$79k/month; implied contribution margin to your $120k ARR pilot ~34% before S&M and infra.
- Summaries (20% = 6M): cost ~$18k/month; personalization (20% = 6M): cost ~$18k/month.

Observations: to get feature margin >40% at pilot scale we either need (a) reduce target $/1M to ~ $3.6k via more aggressive optimization, or (b) increase revenue assumptions for pilot (higher ARR or additional monetization per user). We'll call out the tradeoffs in the workbook.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached unit_econ_model.xlsx and redwood-pricing-proposal.pdf.
2) Confirm a 30-min review slot next week — propose Tue 2026-07-07 10:00am PT or Wed 2026-07-08 11:00am PT.
3) If you can, add peak concurrency info and any telemetry we can use for realistic batching assumptions.

Attachments: unit_econ_model.xlsx, redwood-pricing-proposal.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to the review.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
